question: Complete: ___ ag foghlaim Gaeilge.
explanation: Tá mé ag foghlaim Gaeilge means “I am learning Irish.” The progressive construction uses tá + ag + verbal noun. Literally: Tá mé ag foghlaim = “am I at learning” (ag = “at”).

question: Complete: Is ___ mé. (I am a teacher.)
explanation: Is múinteoir mé is a standard way to say “I am a teacher.” Literally: Is múinteoir mé = “is a teacher me”.

question: How do you say “I have a book”?
explanation: Irish expresses possession with tá + thing + ag + person: Tá leabhar agam. Literally: Tá leabhar agam = “is a book at me”.

question: Complete: Tá an cat ___ an gcathaoir. (The cat is on the chair.)
explanation: Ar means “on”. Ar an gcathaoir means “on the chair”. Literally: Tá an cat ar an gcathaoir = “is the cat on the chair”.

question: Which is a common Irish greeting?
explanation: Dia duit is a common way to say “hello”. Oíche mhaith means “good night”, and slán means “goodbye”. Literally: Dia duit = “God to you”. Oíche mhaith = “night good”. Slán = “safe”.

question: Complete: Chuaigh mé ___ an siopa. (I went to the shop.)
explanation: Chuig can mean “to” or “towards” and introduces a destination. Literally: Chuaigh mé chuig an siopa = “went I towards the shop”.

question: How do you say “I am tired”?
explanation: Tá tuirse orm is a common expression meaning “I am tired”, literally “tiredness is on me”. Literally: Tá tuirse orm = “is tiredness on me” (orm = ar + mé, “on me”).

question: Complete: ___ sé anseo anois. (He is here now.)
explanation: Tá is the present form of bí. Bhí is past tense, and beidh is future tense. Literally: Tá sé anseo anois = “is he here now”.

question: How do you say “She speaks Irish”?
explanation: The usual word order is verb + subject + object: Labhraíonn sí Gaeilge. Literally: Labhraíonn sí Gaeilge = “speaks she Irish”.

question: Complete: Tá siad ag ___ peile. (They are playing football.)
explanation: After ag in this progressive construction, use the verbal noun: ag imirt. Literally: Tá siad ag imirt peile = “are they at playing of football”.

question: How do you say “We went home”?
explanation: Chuaigh is the past-tense form of téigh, meaning “to go”. Abhaile means “home” when describing movement towards home. Literally: Chuaigh muid abhaile = “went we homewards”.

question: Complete: D’ith mé ___. (I ate the apple.)
explanation: An t-úll means “the apple”. The t- is used before a vowel after the singular definite article. Literally: D’ith mé an t-úll = “ate I the apple”.

question: How do you say “I don’t understand”?
explanation: Ní thuigim means “I don't understand”. The verb form is lenited after ní. Literally: Ní thuigim = “not I-understand” (the -im ending already means “I”).

question: Which means “I am going home now”?
options: Tá mé ag dul abhaile anois.
explanation: Ag dul abhaile means “going home”. Sa bhaile means “at home”, while inné means “yesterday”. Literally: Tá mé ag dul abhaile anois = “am I at going homewards now”.

question: How do you ask “Where are you?”
explanation: Cá bhfuil tú? asks about someone's location. Cad means “what” and cé means “who”. Literally: Cá bhfuil tú? = “where is you?”.

question: Complete: ___ is ainm duit? (What is your name?)
explanation: Cad is ainm duit? is a common way to ask someone's name. Literally: Cad is ainm duit? = “what is name to you?”.

question: Which is a common response to “Go raibh maith agat”?
explanation: Fáilte romhat is a common response meaning “you're welcome”. Literally: Fáilte romhat = “welcome before you”. Go raibh maith agat = “may there be good at you”.

question: Complete: Tá cupán tae ___ an mbord. (There is a cup of tea on the table.)
explanation: Ar an mbord means “on the table”. The form of the noun changes after the preposition and article. Literally: Tá cupán tae ar an mbord = “is a cup of tea on the table”.

question: How do you say “I don’t like coffee”?
explanation: Ní maith liom caife means “I don't like coffee”. Literally: Ní maith liom caife = “not good with me coffee”.

question: Choose the sentence meaning “The children are playing.”
explanation: The progressive construction uses tá + subject + ag + verbal noun. Literally: Tá na páistí ag súgradh = “are the children at playing”.

question: Complete: Bhí mé ___ bhaile inné. (I was at home yesterday.)
explanation: Sa bhaile means “at home”. Bhí is the past form of bí, and inné means “yesterday”. Literally: Bhí mé sa bhaile inné = “was I in-the home yesterday” (sa = i + an).

question: How do you say “I saw the woman”?
explanation: Chonaic mé means “I saw”. Chonaic an bhean mé would mean “The woman saw me”. Literally: Chonaic mé an bhean = “saw I the woman”.

question: Complete: Tá dhá ___ agam. (I have two cats.)
explanation: The noun after dhá is commonly lenited: dhá chat, “two cats”. Literally: Tá dhá chat agam = “is two cat at me” (Irish keeps the noun singular after a number).

question: Which means “the books”?
explanation: Leabhair is the plural of leabhar, and na is used with plural definite nouns. Literally: na leabhair = “the (plural) books”.

question: Complete: Tá mé níos ___ inniu. (I am better today.)
explanation: Níos fearr means “better”. Fearr is the comparative form of maith. Literally: Tá mé níos fearr inniu = “am I more better today”.

question: How do you say “She is older than me”?
options: Tá sí níos sine ná mé.
explanation: Níos sine ná means “older than”. Ná introduces the comparison. Literally: Tá sí níos sine ná mé = “is she more old than me”.

question: Complete: Tá am ___ . (You have time.)
explanation: Agat means “at you” and is used in expressions of possession: tá am agat, “you have time”. Literally: Tá am agat = “is time at you”.

question: How do you say “I can speak a little Irish”?
options: Is féidir liom beagán Gaeilge a labhairt.
Is féidir mé labhairt Gaeilge beagán.
explanation: Is féidir liom is a common construction meaning “I can” or “it is possible for me”. Literally: Is féidir liom beagán Gaeilge a labhairt = “is possible with me a little Irish to speak”.

question: Complete: Ba mhaith liom ___ a ithe. (I'd like to eat something.)
explanation: Rud éigin means “something”; duine éigin means “someone”, and áit éigin means “somewhere”. Literally: Ba mhaith liom rud éigin a ithe = “would-be good with me thing some to eat”.

question: How do you say “I have no money”?
explanation: Níl aon airgead agam means “I have no money”. Irish expresses possession with agam. Literally: Níl aon airgead agam = “is-not any money at me”.

question: Complete: Tá an leabhar an-___. (The book is very interesting.)
explanation: The prefix an- intensifies an adjective and is attached with a hyphen: an-spéisiúil means “very interesting”. Literally: an-spéisiúil = “very-interesting” (an- = “very”).

question: How do you say “I will go tomorrow”?
explanation: Rachaidh is the future form of téigh, “to go”. Amárach means “tomorrow”. Literally: Rachaidh mé amárach = “will-go I tomorrow”.

question: Complete: Nuair a ___ mé óg, bhí mé i mo chónaí sa Ghaeltacht. (When I was young...)
explanation: Bhí is the past form of bí. Nuair a bhí mé óg means “when I was young”. Literally: Nuair a bhí mé óg = “when was I young”.

question: Choose the word meaning “because”.
explanation: Mar means “because”; ach means “but”, and nó means “or”. Literally: mar = “because” (also “as” / “for”).

question: Complete: Tá sé ag obair ___ a dheartháir. (He is working with his brother.)
explanation: Le means “with”. Lena dheartháir means “with his brother”. Literally: Tá sé ag obair lena dheartháir = “is he at working with-his brother” (lena = le + a).

question: How do you say “I gave her the book”?
explanation: Thug mé an leabhar di means “I gave her the book”. Di means “to her”. Literally: Thug mé an leabhar di = “gave I the book to-her”.

question: Complete: Is as ___ mé. (I am from Ireland.)
explanation: Is as Éirinn mé is the standard expression for “I am from Ireland”. Literally: Is as Éirinn mé = “is out-of Ireland me”.

question: How do you ask “What are you doing?”
explanation: Cad atá tú a dhéanamh? asks what someone is doing. Literally: Cad atá tú a dhéanamh? = “what that-is you to do?”.

question: Which word means “here”?
explanation: Anseo means “here”; inné means “yesterday”, and amárach means “tomorrow”. Literally: anseo = “in this (place)”.

question: Which sentence expresses living somewhere for two years, continuing until now?
options: Tá mé i mo chónaí anseo le dhá bhliain.
Bhí mé i mo chónaí anseo dhá bhliain ó shin.
Beidh mé i mo chónaí anseo i gceann dhá bhliain.
explanation: Le dhá bhliain can describe a situation that has continued for two years. Ó shin means “ago”, and i gceann dhá bhliain means “in two years' time”. Literally: Tá mé i mo chónaí anseo le dhá bhliain = “am I in my dwelling here with two years”.

question: Complete: Ní raibh ___ agam. (I had no choice.)
explanation: Ní raibh aon rogha agam means “I had no choice”. Aon rogha means “any choice”. Literally: Ní raibh aon rogha agam = “not was any choice at me”.

question: Which expression means “although”?
explanation: Cé go means “although”; mar means “because”, and má means “if”. Literally: cé go = “though that”.

question: Complete: Tá sí níos airde ___ a deirfiúr. (She is taller than her sister.)
explanation: Ná introduces a comparison: níos airde ná means “taller than”. Literally: Tá sí níos airde ná a deirfiúr = “is she more tall than her sister”.

question: How do you say “I would like a cup of tea”?
options: Is maith liom cupán tae anois.
explanation: Ba mhaith liom expresses “I would like”. Literally: Ba mhaith liom cupán tae = “would-be good with me a cup of tea”.

question: Complete: Dá mbeadh níos mó ama agam, ___ níos mó leabhar. (If I had more time, I would read more books.)
explanation: Léifinn means “I would read”. Dá mbeadh introduces a hypothetical condition. Literally: Dá mbeadh níos mó ama agam, léifinn níos mó leabhar = “if would-be more of-time at me, I-would-read more of-books”.

question: Which expression means “I used to play football”?
options: Ba ghnách liom peil a imirt.
explanation: Ba ghnách liom + verbal noun expresses a habitual past action: “I used to…”. Literally: Ba ghnách liom peil a imirt = “was usual with me football to play”.

question: Complete: Tá súil ___ go mbeidh tú ann. (I hope you'll be there.)
explanation: Tá súil agam means “I hope”. Literally: Tá súil agam = “is hope at me”.

question: Complete: ___ tá am agat, cuir glaoch orm. (If you have time, call me.)
explanation: Má means “if”; nuair means “when”, and cé go means “although”. Literally: Má tá am agat, cuir glaoch orm = “if is time at you, put a call on me”.

question: Complete: Ní hamháin go bhfuil sí cliste, ___ tá sí cineálta freisin. (Not only is she clever, but she is also kind.)
explanation: Ní hamháin ... ach ... freisin means “not only ... but also”. Literally: Ní hamháin go bhfuil sí cliste, ach tá sí cineálta freisin = “not only that is she clever, but is she kind also”.

question: How do you say “I am hungry” in Irish?
explanation: Tá ocras orm means “I am hungry.” Tá tart orm means “I am thirsty,” and tá eagla orm means “I am afraid.” Literally: Tá ocras orm = “is hunger on me”.

question: How do you say “I am thirsty” in Irish?
explanation: Tá tart orm means “I am thirsty.” Irish expresses these feelings using orm, meaning “on me.” Literally: Tá tart orm = “is thirst on me”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I am tired.”
explanation: Tá mé tuirseach means “I am tired.” (Tá tuirse orm is the other common way to say it.) Literally: Tá mé tuirseach = “am I tired”. Tá tuirse orm = “is tiredness on me”.

question: How do you say “I have a cold” in Irish?
explanation: Tá slaghdán orm means “I have a cold” (literally “a cold is on me”). Tá ocras orm means “I am hungry.” Literally: Tá slaghdán orm = “is a cold on me”.

question: Complete: Tá áthas ___ orm. (I am very happy.)
explanation: Tá áthas mór orm means “I am very happy” or “I have great joy.” Tá an-áthas orm is also common. Literally: Tá áthas mór orm = “is joy great on me”.

question: What does “Tá brón orm” mean?
explanation: Tá brón orm literally means “sadness is on me” and is commonly used to express sorrow or say “I'm sorry.” Literally: Tá brón orm = “is sadness on me”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I understand.”
explanation: Tuigim means “I understand.” Feicim means “I see,” and cloisim means “I hear.” Literally: Tuigim = “I-understand”; feicim = “I-see”; cloisim = “I-hear” (the -im ending means “I”).

question: How do you say “I know” in Irish?
explanation: Tá a fhios agam means “I know.” Literally, it expresses that knowledge is known to me. Literally: Tá a fhios agam = “is its knowledge at me”.

question: What does “Níl a fhios agam” mean?
explanation: Níl a fhios agam means “I don't know.” Literally: Níl a fhios agam = “is-not its knowledge at me”.

question: Complete: ___ mise Seán.
explanation: Is mise Seán means “I am Seán.” Is is used in identification sentences. Literally: Is mise Seán = “is me Seán” (mise is the emphatic form of mé).

question: How do you say “She is a teacher” in Irish?
explanation: Is múinteoir í means “She is a teacher.” The pronoun í refers to a female person. Literally: Is múinteoir í = “is teacher she”.

question: How do you say “He is a doctor” in Irish?
explanation: Is dochtúir é means “He is a doctor.” Literally: Is dochtúir é = “is doctor he”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “We are friends.”
explanation: Is cairde muid means “We are friends.” Cairde is the plural of cara, “friend.” Literally: Is cairde muid = “is friends us”.

question: What does “Cá bhfuil tú i do chónaí?” mean?
explanation: Cá bhfuil tú i do chónaí? means “Where do you live?” Literally: Cá bhfuil tú i do chónaí? = “where is you in your dwelling?”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I live in Dublin.”
options: Tá mé ag dul go Baile Átha Cliath.
Tá mé i mo chónaí i mBaile Átha Cliath.
Tá mé as Baile Átha Cliath.
explanation: Tá mé i mo chónaí i mBaile Átha Cliath means “I live in Dublin.” Literally: Tá mé i mo chónaí i mBaile Átha Cliath = “am I in my dwelling in Town-of-the-Hurdle-Ford”.

question: What does “Cad as duit?” mean?
explanation: Cad as duit? is a way to ask “Where are you from?” Literally: Cad as duit? = “what out-of to you?”.

question: Complete: Tá mé ag dul ___ an siopa.
explanation: Tá mé ag dul go dtí an siopa means “I am going to the shop.” Literally: Tá mé ag dul go dtí an siopa = “am I at going to the shop”.

question: What does “Tá mé ag teacht abhaile” mean?
explanation: Tá mé ag teacht abhaile means “I am coming home.” Literally: Tá mé ag teacht abhaile = “am I at coming homewards”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I am going to school.”
options: Tá mé ag dul ar scoil.
Tá mé ag teacht ón scoil.
explanation: Tá mé ag dul ar scoil means “I am going to school.” Literally: Tá mé ag dul ar scoil = “am I at going on school”.

question: What does “Tá mé ag obair sa bhaile” mean?
options: I am going home from work.
I am looking for a house.
explanation: Sa bhaile means “at home,” so the sentence means “I am working at home.” Literally: Tá mé ag obair sa bhaile = “am I at working in-the home”.

question: Complete: Tá sí ag ___ leabhar.
explanation: Tá sí ag léamh leabhar means “She is reading a book.” The progressive uses ag plus the verbal noun. Literally: Tá sí ag léamh leabhar = “is she at reading of a book”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “They are eating.”
explanation: Tá siad ag ithe means “They are eating.” Literally: Tá siad ag ithe = “are they at eating”.

question: What does “Tá sé ag ól uisce” mean?
explanation: Tá sé ag ól uisce means “He is drinking water.” Literally: Tá sé ag ól uisce = “is he at drinking water”.

question: How do you say “I like music” in Irish?
explanation: Is maith liom ceol means “I like music.” Irish uses the construction is maith liom. Literally: Is maith liom ceol = “is good with me music”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Do you like tea?”
explanation: An maith leat tae? means “Do you like tea?” Literally: An maith leat tae? = “is-good with you tea?”.

question: Complete: Is fearr liom tae ___ caife.
explanation: Is fearr liom tae ná caife means “I prefer tea to coffee.” Ná is used in this comparison. Literally: Is fearr liom tae ná caife = “is better with me tea than coffee”.

question: What does “Tá sé níos mó ná mise” mean?
explanation: Níos mó means “bigger” here, and ná introduces the comparison. Literally: Tá sé níos mó ná mise = “is he more big than me” (mó is the comparative of mór, “big”).

question: Choose the correct Irish for “This house is small.”
explanation: Beag means “small.” Teach means “house.” Literally: Tá an teach seo beag = “is the house this small”.

question: What does “Tá an aimsir go hálainn” mean?
explanation: Tá an aimsir go hálainn means “The weather is lovely.” Literally: Tá an aimsir go hálainn = “is the weather lovely(ly)” (go + adjective forms an adverb).

question: How do you say “It is raining” in Irish?
explanation: Tá sé ag cur báistí means “It is raining.” Literally: Tá sé ag cur báistí = “is it at putting of rain”.

question: What does “Tá sé ag cur sneachta” mean?
explanation: Tá sé ag cur sneachta means “It is snowing.” Literally: Tá sé ag cur sneachta = “is it at putting of snow”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “It is sunny.”
explanation: Tá an ghrian ag taitneamh means “The sun is shining.” Literally: Tá an ghrian ag taitneamh = “is the sun at shining”.

question: What does “Tá sé fuar inniu” mean?
explanation: Inniu means “today,” and fuar means “cold.” Literally: Tá sé fuar inniu = “is it cold today”.

question: Complete: Chuaigh mé ___ an obair inné.
explanation: Chuaigh mé go dtí an obair inné means “I went to work yesterday.” Literally: Chuaigh mé go dtí an obair inné = “went I to the work yesterday”.

question: What does “D'ith mé bricfeasta” mean?
explanation: D'ith mé means “I ate.” Bricfeasta means “breakfast.” Literally: D’ith mé bricfeasta = “ate I breakfast”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I saw him yesterday.”
explanation: Chonaic mé é inné means “I saw him yesterday.” Chonaic is the past tense of feic. Literally: Chonaic mé é inné = “saw I him yesterday”.

question: What does “Cheannaigh sí carr nua” mean?
explanation: Cheannaigh sí means “She bought.” Carr nua means “a new car.” Literally: Cheannaigh sí carr nua = “bought she car new”.

question: Complete: ___ mé abhaile go déanach.
explanation: Tháinig mé abhaile go déanach means “I came home late.” Tháinig is the past tense of tar. Literally: Tháinig mé abhaile go déanach = “came I homewards late”.

question: What does “Ní dheachaigh mé amach” mean?
explanation: Ní dheachaigh mé amach means “I didn't go out.” Literally: Ní dheachaigh mé amach = “not went I out”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I will see you tomorrow.”
explanation: Feicfidh mé thú amárach means “I will see you tomorrow.” Literally: Feicfidh mé thú amárach = “will-see I you tomorrow”.

question: What does “Beidh mé ann” mean?
explanation: Beidh mé ann means “I will be there.” Literally: Beidh mé ann = “will-be I there”.

question: Complete: Amárach, ___ sé ag obair.
explanation: Beidh sé ag obair means “He will be working.” Amárach means “tomorrow.” Literally: Beidh sé ag obair = “will-be he at working”.

question: What does “Ní bheidh mé sa bhaile anocht” mean?
options: I won't be at home tonight.
I wasn't at home last night.
explanation: Ní bheidh mé sa bhaile anocht means “I won't be at home tonight.” Literally: Ní bheidh mé sa bhaile anocht = “not will-be I in-the home tonight”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Can you help me?”
options: An bhfuil tú ag cabhrú liom?
explanation: An féidir leat cabhrú liom? means “Can you help me?” Literally: An féidir leat cabhrú liom? = “is possible with you to-help with me?”.

question: What does “Caithfidh mé imeacht” mean?
explanation: Caithfidh mé imeacht means “I have to leave.” Literally: Caithfidh mé imeacht = “must I leave” (caithfidh is the verb used for “must”).

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I want to learn Irish.”
options: Ba mhaith liom Gaeilge a fhoghlaim.
explanation: Ba mhaith liom Gaeilge a fhoghlaim means “I would like to learn Irish.” Literally: Ba mhaith liom Gaeilge a fhoghlaim = “would-be good with me Irish to learn”.

question: What does “Tá orm imeacht anois” mean?
explanation: Tá orm imeacht anois means “I have to leave now.” Literally: Tá orm imeacht anois = “is on me to-leave now”.

question: What does “Níl aon rud agam” mean?
explanation: Níl aon rud agam means “I have nothing.” Literally: Níl aon rud agam = “is-not any thing at me”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Someone is here.”
explanation: Duine éigin means “someone.” Rud éigin means “something.” Literally: Tá duine éigin anseo = “is person some here”.

question: What does “Tá rud éigin mícheart” mean?
explanation: Rud éigin means “something,” and mícheart means “wrong.” Literally: Tá rud éigin mícheart = “is thing some wrong” (mí- = “un-”, ceart = “right”).

question: Complete: Tá an leabhar ___ an mbord.
explanation: Tá an leabhar ar an mbord means “The book is on the table.” Literally: Tá an leabhar ar an mbord = “is the book on the table”.

question: How do you say “The cat is under the table” in Irish?
options: Tá an cat os cionn an bhoird.
Tá an cat ar an mbord.
explanation: Faoin mbord means “under the table.” Literally: Tá an cat faoin mbord = “is the cat under-the table” (faoin = faoi + an).

question: What does “Tá an banc in aice leis an stáisiún” mean?
options: The bank is inside the station.
The bank is near the station.
The bank is behind the station.
explanation: In aice le means “beside” or “near.” Literally: Tá an banc in aice leis an stáisiún = “is the bank in side with the station”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “The dog is in the garden.”
options: Tá an madra ar an ngairdín.
explanation: Sa ghairdín means “in the garden.” Literally: Tá an madra sa ghairdín = “is the dog in-the garden”.

question: What does “Tá an siopa os comhair an tí” mean?
options: The shop is behind the house.
The shop is inside the house.
The shop is in front of the house.
explanation: Os comhair means “in front of.” Literally: Tá an siopa os comhair an tí = “is the shop above face of the house”.

question: Complete: Tá an carr idir an teach agus ___ scoil.
explanation: Idir an teach agus an scoil means “between the house and the school.” Literally: Tá an carr idir an teach agus an scoil = “is the car between the house and the school”.

question: What does “Tá mo mhála liom” mean?
explanation: Mo mhála means “my bag,” and liom means “with me.” Literally: Tá mo mhála liom = “is my bag with me”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Her name is Máire.”
explanation: Is é Máire a hainm is a standard way to say “Her name is Máire.” A hainm means “her name.” Literally: Is é Máire a hainm = “is it Máire her name”.

question: What does “Tá beirt deartháireacha agam” mean?
explanation: Deartháireacha means “brothers,” and beirt is used when counting people. Literally: Tá beirt deartháireacha agam = “is two-people brothers at me”.

question: How do you say “I have one sister” in Irish?
explanation: Tá deirfiúr amháin agam means “I have one sister.” Literally: Tá deirfiúr amháin agam = “is sister one at me”.

question: What does “Is liomsa an leabhar seo” mean?
explanation: Is liomsa an leabhar seo means “This book is mine.” Literally: Is liomsa an leabhar seo = “is with-me (emphatic) the book this”.

question: Complete: Seo ___ chara.
explanation: Seo mo chara means “This is my friend.” Mo causes lenition, so cara becomes chara. Literally: Seo mo chara = “this-is my friend”.

question: What does “Cé leis an peann seo?” mean?
explanation: Cé leis? asks “Whose is it?” Literally: Cé leis an peann seo? = “who with-him the pen this?”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I gave him the book.”
explanation: Thug mé an leabhar dó means “I gave him the book.” Literally: Thug mé an leabhar dó = “gave I the book to-him”.

question: What does “Fuair mé bronntanas” mean?
explanation: Fuair mé means “I got” or “I received.” Bronntanas means “present” or “gift.” Literally: Fuair mé bronntanas = “got I a present”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Please sit down.”
explanation: Suigh síos, le do thoil means “Please sit down.” Literally: Suigh síos, le do thoil = “sit down, with your will”.

question: What does “Éirigh suas!” mean?
explanation: Éirigh suas means “Stand up!” or “Get up!” Literally: Éirigh suas = “rise up”.

question: How do you say “Come in” in Irish?
explanation: Tar isteach means “Come in.” Téigh amach means “Go out.” Literally: Tar isteach = “come inwards”.

question: What does “Fan nóiméad” mean?
explanation: Fan means “wait” or “stay,” and nóiméad means “minute.” Literally: Fan nóiméad = “stay a minute”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Be careful!”
explanation: Bí cúramach means “Be careful.” Literally: Bí cúramach = “be careful”.

question: What does “Ná bí buartha” mean?
explanation: Ná bí buartha means “Don't worry” or “Don't be worried.” Literally: Ná bí buartha = “don’t be worried”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Don't touch that!”
explanation: Ná bain leis sin means “Don't touch that!” Literally: Ná bain leis sin = “don’t touch with that”.

question: What does “Labhair níos moille, le do thoil” mean?
explanation: Níos moille means “more slowly.” Literally: Labhair níos moille, le do thoil = “speak more slowly, with your will”.

question: How do you say “Could you repeat that?” in Irish?
options: An bhféadfá é sin a rá arís?
explanation: An bhféadfá é sin a rá arís? means “Could you say that again?” Literally: An bhféadfá é sin a rá arís? = “would-you-be-able it that to say again?”.

question: What does “Cad is brí leis sin?” mean?
explanation: Cad is brí leis sin? means “What does that mean?” Literally: Cad is brí leis sin? = “what is meaning with that?”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I speak a little Irish.”
explanation: Labhraím means “I speak,” and beagán means “a little.” Literally: Labhraím beagán Gaeilge = “I-speak a-little Irish”.

question: What does “Tá mé ag iarraidh Gaeilge a chleachtadh” mean?
options: I am trying to practise Irish.
explanation: Tá mé ag iarraidh ... a chleachtadh means “I am trying/wanting to practise ...” Literally: Tá mé ag iarraidh Gaeilge a chleachtadh = “am I at seeking Irish to practise”.

question: Complete: Is féidir liom Gaeilge a ___.
explanation: Is féidir liom Gaeilge a labhairt means “I can speak Irish.” After a, use the verbal noun: labhairt. Literally: Is féidir liom Gaeilge a labhairt = “is possible with me Irish to speak”.

question: What does “Tá mé ag foghlaim gach lá” mean?
explanation: Gach lá means “every day.” Literally: Tá mé ag foghlaim gach lá = “am I at learning every day”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I read the newspaper every morning.”
options: Éistim leis an nuachtán gach maidin.
explanation: Léim means “I read” in the present tense. Gach maidin means “every morning.” Literally: Léim an nuachtán gach maidin = “I-read the newspaper every morning”.

question: What does “Éist liom” mean?
explanation: Éist liom means “Listen to me.” Literally: Éist liom = “listen with me”.

question: Complete: Tá mé ag caint ___ mo mháthair.
explanation: Tá mé ag caint le mo mháthair means “I am talking to my mother.” Literally: Tá mé ag caint le mo mháthair = “am I at talking with my mother”.

question: What does “Tá mé ag smaoineamh ort” mean?
explanation: Tá mé ag smaoineamh ort means “I am thinking about you.” Literally: Tá mé ag smaoineamh ort = “am I at thinking on you”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I agree with you.”
explanation: Aontaím leat means “I agree with you.” Literally: Aontaím leat = “I-agree with-you”.

question: What does “Ní aontaím leat” mean?
explanation: Ní aontaím leat means “I don't agree with you.” Literally: Ní aontaím leat = “not I-agree with-you”.

question: Complete: Tá mé sásta ___ an toradh.
explanation: Tá mé sásta leis an toradh means “I am happy with the result.” Literally: Tá mé sásta leis an toradh = “am I satisfied with-the result”.

question: What does “Tá díomá orm” mean?
explanation: Tá díomá orm means “I am disappointed.” Literally: Tá díomá orm = “is disappointment on me”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I am proud of you.”
explanation: Tá mé bródúil asat means “I am proud of you.” Literally: Tá mé bródúil asat = “am I proud out-of-you”.

question: What does “Tá imní orm faoi” mean?
explanation: Tá imní orm faoi means “I am worried about” something. Literally: Tá imní orm faoi = “is worry on me about-it”.

question: Complete: Cé go bhfuil sé ag cur báistí, ___ mé ag dul amach.
explanation: Cé go bhfuil sé ag cur báistí, tá mé ag dul amach means “Although it is raining, I am going out.” Literally: Cé go bhfuil sé ag cur báistí, tá mé ag dul amach = “though that is it at putting of rain, am I at going out”.

question: What does “Má bhíonn am agam, cabhróidh mé leat” mean?
options: I don't have time to help you.
I helped you when I had time.
If I have time, I will help you.
explanation: Má bhíonn am agam, cabhróidh mé leat means “If I have time, I will help you.” Literally: Má bhíonn am agam, cabhróidh mé leat = “if is (habitually) time at me, will-help I with-you”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I stayed at home because I was sick.”
options: D'fhan mé sa bhaile mar bhí mé tinn.
Fanfaidh mé sa bhaile mar tá mé sláintiúil.
Chuaigh mé amach mar bhí mé tinn.
explanation: D'fhan mé sa bhaile means “I stayed at home,” and mar means “because.” Literally: D’fhan mé sa bhaile mar bhí mé tinn = “stayed I in-the home because was I sick”.

question: What does “Sula dtéann tú, glaoigh orm” mean?
options: If you leave, don't call me.
explanation: Sula means “before,” and glaoigh orm means “call me.” Literally: Sula dtéann tú, glaoigh orm = “before that-goes you, call on me”.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I have never been to Galway.”
options: Tá mé i nGaillimh gach lá.
Ní raibh mé riamh i nGaillimh.
explanation: Ní raibh mé riamh i nGaillimh means “I have never been to Galway.” Literally: Ní raibh mé riamh i nGaillimh = “not was I ever in Galway”.

question: What does “Tá súil agam go bhfeicfidh mé thú arís” mean?
options: I don't want to see you again.
I know I saw you yesterday.
I hope I will see you again.
explanation: Tá súil agam means “I hope,” and go bhfeicfidh mé thú arís means “that I will see you again.” Literally: Tá súil agam go bhfeicfidh mé thú arís = “is hope at me that will-see I you again”.

question: What does “a cúig” mean?
explanation: A cúig is the counting form of “five”. Trí is “three” and seacht is “seven”.

question: Which Irish word means “ten”?
explanation: Deich means “ten”. Fiche means “twenty” and seacht means “seven”.

question: What does “fiche” mean?
explanation: Fiche means “twenty”. “Twelve” is dhá dheag and “one hundred” is céad.

question: What is “Monday” in Irish?
explanation: Dé Luain is Monday. Dé Máirt is Tuesday and Dé hAoine is Friday. Literally: Dé Luain = “day of the Moon” (luan = moon).

question: What does “Dé Sathairn” mean?
explanation: Dé Sathairn is Saturday. Dé Domhnaigh is Sunday and Dé hAoine is Friday. Literally: Dé Sathairn = “day of Saturn”.

question: What does “dearg” mean?
explanation: Dearg means “red”. Glas is “green” and gorm is “blue”.

question: Choose the Irish word for “green”.
explanation: Glas means “green”. Gorm is “blue” and buí is “yellow”.

question: What does “bán” mean?
explanation: Bán means “white”. Dubh is “black” and buí is “yellow”.

question: How do you say “my brother” in Irish?
explanation: Mo causes lenition, so deartháir becomes dheartháir. Mo dheirfiúr means “my sister”. Literally: mo dheartháir = “my brother” (the d softens to dh after mo).

question: What does “arán” mean?
explanation: Arán means “bread”. Im is “butter” and bainne is “milk”.

question: What does “uibheacha” mean?
explanation: Uibheacha is the plural of ubh, “egg”. Cáis is “cheese” and iasc is “fish”.

question: What does “Cén t-am é?” mean?
explanation: Cén t-am é? asks the time. Cén lá é? would ask the day. Literally: Cén t-am é? = “what time is-it?”.

question: How do you say “It is one o'clock” in Irish?
options: Tá sé a naoi a chlog.
Tá sé a haon a chlog.
Tá sé a trí a chlog.
explanation: Tá sé a haon a chlog means “It is one o'clock”. The other options give three and nine o'clock. Literally: Tá sé a haon a chlog = “is it one of-the-bell (o’clock)” (clog = bell).

question: What does “ceann” mean?
explanation: Ceann means “head”. Lámh is “hand” and cos is “foot”.

question: What does “Tá pian i mo chos” mean?
options: I have a pain in my head.
I have a pain in my hand.
I have a pain in my foot.
explanation: Cos means “foot”, and it is lenited after mo: i mo chos. Literally: Tá pian i mo chos = “is pain in my foot”.

question: What does “ar chlé” mean?
explanation: Ar chlé means “on the left”. Ar dheis is “on the right” and díreach ar aghaidh is “straight ahead”. Literally: ar chlé = “on left”.

question: How do you say “Turn right” in Irish?
explanation: Cas ar dheis means “Turn right”. Cas ar chlé means “Turn left”. Literally: Cas ar dheis = “turn on right”.

question: Which Irish word means “January”?
explanation: Eanáir is January. Feabhra is February and Márta is March.

question: What does “Meitheamh” mean?
explanation: Meitheamh is June. Bealtaine is May and Iúil is July.

question: What does “samhradh” mean?
explanation: Samhradh is “summer”. Geimhreadh is “winter” and earrach is “spring”.

question: Which Irish word means “autumn”?
explanation: Fómhar is “autumn”. Earrach is “spring” and samhradh is “summer”.

question: Complete: An ___ tú ag obair? (Are you working?)
explanation: Questions use an + the eclipsed form bhfuil: An bhfuil tú ag obair? Literally: An bhfuil tú ag obair? = “is you at working?”.

question: What is the usual answer meaning “yes” to “An bhfuil tú ag obair?”
explanation: Irish answers a yes/no question by repeating the verb: An bhfuil...? → Tá (yes) or Níl (no). Is ea / Ní hea answer questions with is. Literally: Tá = “is”; Níl = “is-not”; Is ea = “is it”; Ní hea = “is-not it”.

question: What does “Bím ag obair gach lá” mean?
explanation: Bím is the habitual present of bí and describes something that happens regularly. Literally: Bím ag obair gach lá = “I-am (habitually) at working every day”.

question: How do you say “I close the door” in Irish?
explanation: Dúnaim means “I close”. Osclaím means “I open” and cnagaim means “I knock”. Literally: Dúnaim an doras = “I-close the door”.

question: What does “Dún an doras” mean?
explanation: Dún is the imperative of dún, “to close”.

question: Which means “the door of the house”?
explanation: After a noun, the genitive of teach with the article is an tí: doras an tí. Literally: doras an tí = “door of-the house”.

question: What is the plural of “teach” (house)?
explanation: Tithe is the plural of teach.

question: Which means “the boys”?
explanation: Buachaillí is the plural of buachaill, and na is the plural article. Literally: na buachaillí = “the boys” (buachaill literally means “cow-herd”, from bó = cow).

question: Choose the Irish for “her house”.
explanation: A (her) causes no mutation: a teach. A (his) lenites (a theach) and a (their) eclipses (a dteach). Literally: a teach = “her house”.

question: Choose the Irish for “my mother”.
explanation: Mo lenites the next consonant: mo mháthair. Ár means “our”. Literally: mo mháthair = “my mother”.

question: Which means “with you” (one person)?
explanation: Leat means “with you”. Leis is “with him” and linn is “with us”. Literally: leat = “with-you” (le + tú).

question: Which means “on him”?
explanation: Air means “on him”. Uirthi is “on her” and orm is “on me”. Literally: air = “on-him” (ar + é).

question: How do you ask “How are you?” in Irish?
explanation: Conas atá tú? means “How are you?” Cad is ainm duit? asks for a name. Literally: Conas atá tú? = “how that-is you?”.

question: How do you say “I'm well, thank you”?
options: Is mise Seán, go raibh maith agat.
Tá mé go dona, go raibh maith agat.
Tá mé go maith, go raibh maith agat.
explanation: Go maith means “well”. Go dona means “badly”. Literally: Tá mé go maith, go raibh maith agat = “am I well, may-be good at you”.

question: What does “Slán abhaile” mean?
explanation: Slán abhaile is a friendly goodbye wishing someone a safe journey home. Literally: Slán abhaile = “safe homewards”.

question: Which means “Good morning”?
explanation: Maidin mhaith is “good morning”. Tráthnóna maith is “good afternoon/evening” and oíche mhaith is “good night”. Literally: Maidin mhaith = “morning good”.

question: What does “Go n-éirí leat” mean?
explanation: Go n-éirí leat means “may you succeed”, used to say good luck. Literally: Go n-éirí leat = “that may-succeed with you”.

question: What does “Lá breithe sona duit” mean?
explanation: Lá breithe sona duit means “happy birthday”. Nollaig shona duit means “happy Christmas”. Literally: Lá breithe sona duit = “day of-birth happy to you”.

question: Complete: ___ raibh mé ann. (I wasn't there.)
explanation: Ní raibh is the negative past of bí. Níl is the negative present. Literally: Ní raibh mé ann = “not was I there”.

question: What does “Nach bhfuil tú sásta?” mean?
explanation: Nach bhfuil...? is the negative question form, meaning “isn't/aren't...?” Literally: Nach bhfuil tú sásta? = “is-not-that you satisfied?”.

question: What does “Ní raibh sé fuar” mean?
explanation: Ní raibh is the negative past of bí, so the sentence is in the past tense. Literally: Ní raibh sé fuar = “not was it cold”.

question: Complete: Má ___ an aimsir go maith, rachaidh mé amach. (If the weather is good, I'll go out.)
explanation: After má, the present tense of bí is used for a future-looking condition: Má tá an aimsir go maith... Literally: Má tá an aimsir go maith = “if is the weather good”.

question: What does “Teastaíonn uisce uaim” mean?
explanation: Teastaíonn ... uaim means “I need/want ...”. Literally: Teastaíonn uisce uaim = “is-needed water from me”.

question: What does “Cathain” mean?
explanation: Cathain means “when”. Cén fáth is “why” and conas is “how”.

question: Which question word means “why”?
explanation: Cén fáth means “why”. Cathain is “when” and conas is “how”. Literally: Cén fáth = “what the reason”.

question: What does “Cé mhéad?” mean?
explanation: Cé mhéad? asks about quantity or price. Literally: Cé mhéad? = “what amount?”.

question: What does “Cén aois thú?” mean?
explanation: Cén aois thú? asks someone's age. Literally: Cén aois thú? = “what age you?”.

question: What does “Gabh mo leithscéal” mean?
explanation: Gabh mo leithscéal means “excuse me” or “pardon me”. Literally: Gabh mo leithscéal = “take my excuse”.

question: How do you say “Thank you very much”?
explanation: Go raibh míle maith agat means “thank you very much”. Go raibh maith agat is plain “thank you”. Literally: Go raibh míle maith agat = “may-be a-thousand good at you”.
